summary: Manual slice 'Hash-view of outputs' and 'Hash-view of computation' (doc/README.md 8569-9363) checked sentence by sentence against src/cartesi/hash-tree.lua, the C++ collectors and back_merkle_tree, the CLI computation-hash builders, libcmt's outputs tree, the pinned rollups-contracts output and machine validity proofs, and Dave's Commitment/Tree/CartesiStateTransition. No contradiction with a security consequence above Low/Medium-by-stand-in was found. Every formula, padding rule, height and printed figure that I could test held: 13/13 code excerpts of the slice are byte-identical to the sources; the fixed-point-tree figure (16 of 31 nodes: 6,4,3,2,1) and the outputs-tree figure (6+3 outputs, 7 pristine as 4+2+1) match; libcmt's 65-entry pristine table equals keccak doubling of 32 zero bytes; the collectors and the CLI agree with a from-scratch reference built only from run/run_uarch/reset_uarch/get_root_hash on accept, reject, halt, exception, oversized (no-op) delivery and empty-epoch scenarios. Two minor candidates are reported for triage.

candidates.title: The manual's output verifier (verify-output-proof.lua) and the CLI's read_proof execute proof files as Lua chunks: a crafted proof hangs the verifier or makes it allocate without bound
candidates.component: doc/recipes/verify-output-proof.lua (the script printed in the manual under 'Output verification', doc/README.md 8914-8982) and src/cartesi-machine.lua read_proof (default proof format 'lua', used for --cmio-advance-state=last_output_proof)
candidates.role: Support (manual recipe and cartesi-machine CLI). The recipe is a copy of the referee's output validation (A5), so it stands in for a referee verifier; the CLI stands in for the honest operator.
candidates.location: doc/recipes/verify-output-proof.lua: read_proof (lines 11-13 of the recipe, 'assert(loadfile(name, "t", {}))()'), manual doc/README.md 8924-8927 and 8946-8949; src/cartesi-machine.lua 1317-1324 (resolve_format defaults to 'lua'), 3374-3385 (serialize_proof writes 'return {...}'), 3446-3450 (read_proof: 'assert(load(contents, filename, "t", {}))()'), 3535-3541 (last_output_proof)
candidates.description: The manual presents verify-output-proof.lua as the way to check an output 'from the settled state hash and those artifacts alone, without instantiating any machine', and the script treats every field of the two proofs as adversarial (it checks root, tree height, target size, address and index range before verify_slice). But the proofs themselves are not parsed as data: read_proof runs the proof file as Lua source with loadfile(name, 't', {}) and takes whatever the chunk returns. The empty environment removes the globals, but not the language: a proof file may loop forever, and the string metatable still reaches string.rep/format/gsub, so it may also allocate without bound. The CLI has the same reader: its default proof format is a Lua chunk ('return {...}', resolve_format returns 'lua' unless the name ends in .json or format:json is given) and read_proof load()s the file given as last_output_proof. I found no sandbox escape and no soundness break (tables cannot carry metatables, fields from separate files cannot alias, floats and tables in place of integers and strings are refused by verify_slice, keccak256's two-argument form refuses non-hash sizes), so the effect is a hang or unbounded allocation in the verifier, before any check of the proof runs. The safe decoder already exists (cartesi.fromjson(contents, 'Proof') under format:json).
candidates.trigger: Whoever hands an output proof or an outputs-Merkle-root proof to a party that verifies it with the manual's script (or a last-output proof to an operator who resumes an epoch with the CLI's default format). A one-line file such as 'while true do end' or 'return { iflags_y_data = ("x"):rep(1 << 34) }' is enough.
candidates.reachability: Needs the verifying party to take a proof file from another party, which is the purpose of an output proof (the prover is the one who wants the output accepted). In the manual's own walk-through the files are the reader's own artifacts, written by the CLI in the same session; in that use nothing adversarial reaches the loader. No machine state is involved.

rating_steps.1_out_of_scope: Not excluded. It does not need 'an untrusted party to call the machine API directly'; the data is a proof file, and section 4 says 'Logs and proofs are adversarial. A verifier must assume that every count, index, address, size, and hash it receives was chosen to fool it.'
rating_steps.2_role: Support: AUDIT.md lists 'The PRT player and bridge in doc/recipes, the cartesi-machine CLI, and the Lua helper libraries' as Support. Section 3: 'A defect that only a support component shows is Medium when it would rate High or Critical in the role the component stands in for, such as a referee verifier for a copy of a verifier ... Any other support defect is Low.' The recipe copies the referee's output validation (A5: 'An output is accepted only through a proof that authenticates a hash as a leaf of the full-height outputs tree').
rating_steps.3_high_medium_cases: In the stood-in role this is an unbounded verifier on data from other parties: section 4 'Every path that carries such data must be memory-safe and bounded, and must report errors without terminating the process', and High lists 'A crash, hang, memory-safety defect or unbounded allocation in a component in the honest-operator role, caused by data from other parties that the honest operator may decline' (section 4: the operator 'may decline logs and proofs that it only verifies for its own information'). That gives Medium for the support copy by 'A defect that only a support component shows, when section 3 rates it Medium.'
rating_steps.4_critical: Not Critical: no referee verifier, referee model or honest-operator component shows it. The PRT referee model and players receive proofs as JSON under the 'Proof' schema (prtu.lua SCHEMA_DICT), and the deployed referee takes typed calldata.
rating_steps.5_low: Alternative reading, which I think triage may prefer: Low, if the script and the CLI option are read as consuming only artifacts the same operator wrote ('a failure that needs misuse of an API by its trusted caller'), since the walk-through never exchanges the files.

candidates.claimed_severity: Medium (preferred reading: the manual's output verifier stands in for the referee's output validation and is unbounded on an adversarial proof) / Low (if its inputs are only the operator's own artifacts)
candidates.threat_to_goal: It does not break the goal of section 1: no wrong output is accepted and no honest claim is lost. It violates the trust-boundary rule of section 4 for a verifier of proofs in a component the manual offers as the reference way to check outputs: the party that should be convinced by a proof instead executes it.
candidates.evidence: Ran lua5.4 doc/recipes/verify-output-proof.lua hash.bin loop.lua empty.lua out.bin with loop.lua = 'while true do end': no output, killed by timeout 5 (exit 124). With big.lua = 'return { iflags_y_data = ("x"):rep(1 << 34) }' under ulimit -v 4000000: 'not enough memory' (exit 1); without a limit it allocates 16 GiB. Both happen inside read_proof, before any assert of the script. Files in the scratch directory under vop/.
candidates.test_idea: bugs/<ID>/test.sh: write a proof file containing 'while true do end' (and a second one that builds a 2^34-byte string), run the manual's verify-output-proof.lua on it under 'timeout 10' and a ulimit -v; required behavior is a prompt rejection (non-zero exit with an error message, before the timeout, without exceeding the memory limit); exit 1 if the run times out or dies of memory exhaustion, 0 if it rejects. A second case does the same for cartesi-machine --cmio-advance-state=last_output_proof:<file> with the default format.

candidates.title: frontier_forest refuses the heights the manual says it shares with frontier (63 and above), so the documented last-output proof of the 63-level outputs tree cannot build a forest
candidates.component: Lua helper library cartesi.hash-tree (frontier_forest), against the manual's 'Frontier forests' section
candidates.role: Support (AUDIT.md: 'the frontier and forest functions of cartesi.hash-tree')
candidates.location: src/cartesi/hash-tree.lua frontier_forest lines 780-787 ('unsupported forest height' unless 0 <= height < 63); manual doc/README.md 9166-9172 ('The constructor is frontier_forest, which takes the same height and hash type as frontier and returns an empty forest. Like frontier, it also accepts a proof of the last appended leaf instead of a height, verifies it, and restores coverage through that leaf.') and 8576-8577 (outputs tree height fixed at 63)
candidates.description: The manual states that frontier_forest takes the same height as frontier and, like frontier, a proof of the last appended leaf. frontier accepts any height (the module handles 63, 64 and 'trees taller than a Lua integer'), and its documented proof argument is the last output proof of the outputs tree, whose log2_root_size is 63. frontier_forest asserts height < 63, so both frontier_forest(63, ...) and frontier_forest(<last output proof>, ...) fail with 'unsupported forest height'. The limit is only stated in a source comment ('Heights stay below 63 so counts and indices remain positive Lua integers. A taller tree splits into bundle forests under an outer forest'). The same limit means an mcycle claim forest (height 72 - p in prt.lua's builder) cannot be built for a sampling period below 2^10 mcycles, which the manual's recipes (p = 10, height 62, the maximum) and the released Dave geometry (p = 18, height 54) do not hit.
candidates.trigger: Any caller that follows the manual and builds a forest over the outputs tree (height 63) or over a computation tree taller than 62 levels.
candidates.reachability: Deterministic for those heights; fails loudly at construction. Not reached by the recipes or by the pinned Dave geometry.

rating_steps.2_role: Support library. 'A library stands in for the most critical role among the components that reach the defect through it': no component in the repository reaches it (the outputs tree is only handled with frontiers; claim forests are at most 62 levels).
rating_steps.3_high_medium_cases: 'A contradiction between the manual and the behavior on a security-relevant point is a defect in one of the two. It takes the severity it would have if the manual were right.' If the manual were right, the defect is a support library refusing a documented argument, loudly, with no wrong hash or proof. That matches no High or Medium case.
rating_steps.4_critical: No rule or obligation is violated at a reachable state or on the honest operator's path.
rating_steps.5_low: Low: 'a real defect that violates no rule or obligation of this model'.

candidates.threat_to_goal: None to the goal. It is a contradiction between the manual and the library on a limit (R13 lists the computation-hash construction as part of the protocol, but the limit only makes the support library refuse, never miscompute).
candidates.evidence: lua5.4: pcall(hash_tree.frontier_forest, 63, 'keccak256') -> false, 'hash-tree.lua:784: unsupported forest height'; the same error for frontier_forest(p, 'keccak256') where p is the proof returned by frontier_next_proofs on a height-63 frontier, which hash_tree.frontier(p, 'keccak256') accepts.
candidates.test_idea: test.lua: build a height-63 frontier, take the last proof from frontier_next_proofs, and assert that frontier_forest accepts what frontier accepts (or that the manual states the limit); today the forest constructor raises.

checked_and_consistent: Manual code excerpts of the slice (13 blocks) are byte-identical to src/cartesi/hash-tree.lua and doc/recipes/verify-output-proof.lua.

cartesi.hash-tree forests: randomized differential test against a naive full tree (heights 0-7, nesting depth 2, raw hashes at any aligned height, nested and padded forests, push/append/pad in every pending-merge combination, store/load round trips, expansions of opaque nodes in random order with partially opaque replacements, reload after expansion): roots, every node hash and every sibling path agree over about 215,000 node queries in 8 seeds. The only failure seen is the already known R4-RGPROOF-1 class (expand_leaf 'leaf height mismatch' on a node that a store/load made fully known); it never occurred without store/load.

cartesi.hash-tree at large heights: forest versus frontier roots under identical push/append/pad sequences at heights 1-62 with counts up to 2^62, proofs from the forest verified with verify_slice, frontier_pad_back(count) versus frontier_get_root_hash(pad), 2000 trees: no mismatch. Frontier at heights 63 and 64 with leaf counts next to 2^62, 2^63 and 2^64: pad_back, get_leaf_count, next_proofs, frontier(proof) and the overflow refusals all correct (900 trials).

Mcycle and uarch cycle computation hashes: a reference built only from send_cmio_response, run, run_uarch, reset_uarch and get_root_hash plus an independent run-length Merkle root, following the manual's definitions (leaf k is the state after k periods from the delivery, leaves past a stop repeat the stop's hash or the reverted hash, leaves past the last input repeat the final hash; uarch leaves are the state after each uarch cycle, then the halted state, then the state after reset, and at a fixed point the tail of the canonical state repeats). cartesi-machine --mcycle-computation-hash (bundle 0 and 3) and --uarch-cycle-computation-hash (bundle 16, 0 and 7; periods at the start of an input, at, before and after the stop, the last period of an input, and periods of input slots with no input) equal the reference in scenarios accept, reject as last input, reject in the middle, halt, exception yield, input larger than the rx buffer, and the empty epoch.

collect_mcycle_root_hashes with bundles 0-6, random and bundle-aligned chunk ends, carried phase and partial bundle: bundle roots, entry counts, the pad-only last entry, final_bundle_sibling_hashes (present exactly when the stop completes a bundle or is a fixed point, and proving hashes[#hashes] or hashes[#hashes-1] as the manual says) and collect_mcycle_bundle all match naive samples.

collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes with bundle sizes 0, 1, 5, 12, 16, 19, 20 and random: per-mcycle roots rebuilt with the documented convention (execution entries, halt entry as pad value possibly zero times, reset-ending entry) equal the naive 2^20-leaf root for an ordinary mcycle, the first mcycle after delivery, the rejecting mcycle followed by the revert tail, halt and exception fixed points; collect_uarch_cycle_bundle leaves match too.

Outputs tree: libcmt merkle.c height 63, zero pristine leaf and all 65 precomputed pristine hashes equal keccak doubling; leaf is keccak256 of the emitted bytes; rollups-contracts 3.0.0-alpha.10 validateOutputHash requires exactly 63 siblings and nodeIndex >> 63 == 0, LibMachineValidityProof authenticates iflags.Y != 0, the manual-yield rx-accepted tohost and the tx-buffer leaf in the same machine root; the manual's script and doc/recipes/game-output.lua make the same checks (root, 64-level machine tree, word target, address, 63-level outputs tree, leaf target, index range).

Dave Commitment.getRoot/getRootForLastLeaf require treeHeight siblings (leaf authenticated at height zero); CartesiStateTransition maps counter to delivery+step, step, and step+reset as the manual's uarch leaf layout requires; released geometry 54+38 = 24+48+20.
not_covered: The imcyclemax fixed point inside an input (a guest that runs its whole 2^48-mcycle span) was not executed; it was only reasoned about from interpret() and get_state_break_reason.

The PRT player's own builders in doc/recipes/prt.lua (forests with final-bundle proofs, bundle opening, restart persistence) were read but not run against the naive reference; only the CLI builders and the emulator's collectors were.

Uarch runs close to 2^20 cycles per mcycle (the case where the halt pad count is zero, or the collector's execution_bundle_count assert) cannot be produced with real guests and were only reasoned about for bundle sizes 19 and 20.
sha256 forests and frontiers, frontier_store/frontier_load round trips, verify_splice, and crash-interrupted frontier_forest_store were not tested.
Nothing was run on the chain or EVM harness: Dave's Commitment/Tree libraries and the rollups-contracts output validation were compared with the manual by reading only.

libcmt was read at the tag from a source tree left by an earlier hunter of this campaign (no .git to confirm the tag); the guest binaries in the rootfs were not compared with it, and nothing was run inside a machine with libcmt.
The JSON-RPC path of the collectors was exercised only through the CLI's --remote-spawn runs; the C API was not called directly.

The mcycle computation hash for sampling periods below 2^10 with the PRT player (forest height above 62) and CLI trees taller than 63 levels were only run for the uarch options (the CLI printed its 'height 70 exceeds 63' warning and still matched the reference).
